solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Run racket with agent from the other side (7)

indicators.note: the agent is read from the far end, so the letters come backwards

blocks.note: a racket is a swindle, a scam
a rep is a sales agent; turned round it gives PER

annotation.surface: A gangster flees a crooked scheme with a spy who has changed sides.
annotation.walkthrough: 'From the other side' sounds like a defecting agent, but it only asks you to read REP backwards.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to scamper is a particular way of running, quick and light-footed, like a child or a small animal.

entries.clue: Band abruptly vacated parade (6)

indicators.note: emptying 'abruptly' of its contents leaves only its first and last letters

blocks.note: a sash is a band of cloth worn over the shoulder
A…Y, the outside letters of ABRUPTLY

annotation.surface: A marching band suddenly deserts the parade ground.
annotation.walkthrough: Band and parade suggest a military procession; here parade is a verb, to strut showily.
annotation.definitionFit: To sashay is to walk in a showy, swaggering way, to parade.

entries.clue: Patriarch advanced with supporter on poor player (7)

blocks.note: A is the standard abbreviation for advanced
a bra is a supporting undergarment
a ham is a bad, overacting actor

annotation.surface: An aged head of the family steps forward to back a struggling sportsman.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Supporter' and 'player' suggest a football fan and a footballer; they are a garment and a hammy actor.
annotation.definitionFit: Abraham is the first of the Old Testament patriarchs.

entries.clue: Ancient royal author to seem boring? (9)

blocks.note: to author a text is to pen it
DRAG ON: to seem boringly long

annotation.surface: An old king sets out to write something so dull it tires the reader.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Author' looks like a noun, a writer, but here it is the verb to write. Uther Pendragon was the legendary British king, father of Arthur.
annotation.definitionFit: Pendragon was the title of ancient British chief kings, most famously Uther Pendragon.

entries.clue: Vessel floating right back (4)

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for right
aft is the back of a ship

annotation.surface: A boat drifts straight back to shore.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Back' tempts you to reverse something, but it is simply AFT, the nautical word for the rear.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: planks or logs lashed together float on water and carry people, making the humblest kind of vessel.

entries.clue: Expend power during strike (7)

indicators.note: P comes during, that is inside, the word for strike

blocks.note: to strike out words is to delete them
P is the symbol for power in physics

annotation.surface: A report on energy use while workers are out on strike.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Strike' paints an industrial dispute; it means to strike out, as with a pen.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: spending resources until little remains is exactly what depleting them means, as with savings or energy reserves.

entries.clue: Varying info these days to support one taking the plunge? (10)

definitions.note: 'Varying' used as a noun (the act of varying), matching the noun DIVERGENCE

indicators.note: in a down answer, a supporting piece holds up what sits above it, so GEN and CE go underneath

blocks.note: a diver literally plunges into water
gen is British slang for information
CE = Common Era, the present era of dates

annotation.surface: Changing news of the moment encourages someone about to make a big decision.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Taking the plunge' reads as committing to something bold, such as marriage, but here it is a literal dive into water.
annotation.definitionFit: Divergence is the act of varying or differing from a norm.

entries.clue: Overly proper round university religious festival (5)

indicators.note: to go round something is to surround it, so PRIM encircles U

blocks.note: prim = stiffly formal and proper
U is the abbreviation for university

annotation.surface: A stuffy academic celebration held on campus.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Round' can look like a noun, a round of drinks, but it is the instruction to wrap one word around another.
annotation.definitionFit: Purim is a Jewish festival commemorating the deliverance told in the Book of Esther.

entries.clue: Implicate sibling cutting tree up (7)

indicators.note: BRO cuts into the tree, sitting inside it
in a down answer the tree is written upwards, reversed

blocks.note: the lime is a tree; reversed it reads EMIL
bro is short for brother

annotation.surface: Someone accuses their brother of chopping down the family tree.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a sibling felling a tree; the tree is turned upside down and the brother sits inside it.
annotation.definitionFit: To embroil someone is to drag them into a conflict, to implicate them.

entries.clue: Ability to notice each delight before you (5,3)

blocks.note: ea. is the abbreviation for each
glee = joy, delight
ye is the old form of you

indicators.note: GLEE comes before YE in the answer

annotation.surface: A skill for spotting everyone's pleasure before they show it to you.
annotation.walkthrough: YE is the archaic plural of you, a crossword staple; 'each' is the usual abbreviation EA.
annotation.definitionFit: An eagle eye is keen sight, a sharp ability to notice detail.

entries.clue: Two leaders in Spanish gang always behind loud seasonal unrest (6,5)

indicators.note: take the first two letters of Spanish
to be behind something is to follow it, so the word for always comes after the letter for loud

blocks.note: the first two letters of SPANISH, its two leaders
a ring is a gang, as in a smuggling ring
f = forte, loud in music
ever = always

annotation.surface: A Spanish gang's chiefs have always stirred up trouble each spring.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Leaders' suggests the gang bosses of the surface; it means first letters. F for loud comes from forte in musical scores.
annotation.definitionFit: Spring fever is the restlessness that is said to come with spring.

entries.clue: Shoot crow, missing rook (3)

indicators.note: the word for crow is missing R

blocks.note: to crow is to boast, to brag
R is the chess abbreviation for rook; removed

annotation.surface: A hunter shoots a crow but misses the rook beside it.
annotation.walkthrough: Crow and rook look like two birds on a shoot; crow is the verb to boast, and rook is a chess piece.
annotation.definitionFit: A hunting sense: a shooter who kills game birds puts them in the game bag, so bagging them means shooting them.

entries.clue: Some flash or éclat on the beach (6)

indicators.note: the answer is some of the words that follow

blocks.note: fl(ASH OR É)clat

annotation.surface: A burst of showy brilliance on the seaside.
annotation.walkthrough: The accent on É is ignored, as accents always are in crosswords.
annotation.definitionFit: Ashore means on land, on the beach rather than at sea.

entries.clue: Breaking norm to be music producer (8)

indicators.note: the letters are broken up and reassembled

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 8 letters

annotation.surface: A record producer defying convention.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Music producer' suggests a person in a studio; it is an instrument, which literally produces music.
annotation.definitionFit: A trombone is a brass instrument, something that produces music.

entries.clue: Seeming old and wise, acquiring Tesla (10)

indicators.note: the word for wise acquires T, taking it inside

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old
sensible = wise
T is the SI symbol for the tesla, the unit of magnetic flux density

annotation.surface: An apparently experienced elder takes over the electric car company.
annotation.walkthrough: Tesla invites thoughts of cars or Nikola Tesla; it is the physics unit, symbol T.
annotation.definitionFit: Ostensible means apparent, seeming, as in the ostensible reason.

entries.clue: Significantly, soldiers intervening with authority (13)

indicators.note: the soldiers come between letters of the first word

blocks.note: materially = significantly, to a significant degree
GIs are American soldiers

annotation.surface: Troops step in to take charge in a big way.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is the last phrase; 'Significantly' at the front looks like it ought to be, but it is the container.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a magistrate or master speaks with command, and the adverb describes behaving in that authoritative way.

entries.clue: Mock restraint after blowing top (9)

indicators.note: the word loses its top letter, the first in a down answer

blocks.note: a limitation is a restraint; drop the L

annotation.surface: Someone ridicules self-control just after losing their temper.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Blowing top' reads as losing your temper, but it just removes the first letter. Mock is the adjective here, as in mock leather.
annotation.definitionFit: Mock as an adjective means imitation, not genuine.

entries.clue: Sweet rice came curried (3,5)

indicators.note: made into a curry, the letters are mixed up

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 8 letters

annotation.surface: A dessert of rice turned up in a curry.
annotation.walkthrough: A sweet here is a British dessert, a pudding.
annotation.definitionFit: A British usage: the sweet is the dessert course, and a frozen dairy treat is one of the commonest things served as it.

entries.clue: Domino effect set off in new chaotic era (5,8)

indicators.note: the letters are set off, sent in a new arrangement

blocks.note: used as is
N is the abbreviation for new
anagram fodder, 10 letters

annotation.surface: Toppling dominoes spark off a new age of chaos.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Chaotic' looks like the anagram indicator, but it is fodder; 'set off' does the mixing.
annotation.definitionFit: A domino effect is a chain reaction, one event triggering the next.

entries.clue: Desert wildness (7)

blocks.note: the verb: to leave someone in the lurch
a noun: complete lack of restraint, as in dancing with wild ___

annotation.surface: The untamed wilderness of a desert.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Desert' reads as the sandy noun; it is the verb to leave behind.
annotation.definitionFit: Abandon means both to desert and uninhibited wildness.

entries.clue: Tusker charged over wife? Well, almost (7)

indicators.note: in a down answer, over turns RAN upside down
the word for well is almost complete, losing its last letter

blocks.note: charged = ran at; turned over gives NAR
W is the abbreviation for wife
hale = well, healthy; almost gives HAL

annotation.surface: An elephant charges at a man's wife, and she is almost unhurt.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tusker' suggests an elephant; the narwhal's long spiral tusk makes it one too.
annotation.definitionFit: The narwhal is an Arctic whale whose male has a long tusk.

entries.clue: Unsavoury type tailed and carried out (6)

indicators.note: the word for type has its tail cut off

blocks.note: sort = type; tailed, it loses its last letter
did = carried out, performed

annotation.surface: A shady character is followed and then carried out of the building.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tailed' reads as followed by a detective; here it means having the tail removed.
annotation.definitionFit: Sordid means morally unsavoury, squalid.

entries.clue: Crustaceans fail to nip provided you initially retreated (8)

indicators.note: the word for fail nips, grips, the other letters inside it
take the first letter of you
an army that has retreated has gone backwards, so IF and Y are written in reverse order

blocks.note: a computer that crashes fails
provided = if
its first letter

annotation.surface: Lobster-like creatures miss their chance to pinch you as you back off.
annotation.walkthrough: The nipping claws of crustaceans make the surface feel natural, but 'nip' is the container instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: Crayfish are freshwater crustaceans; the plural is the same as the singular.

entries.clue: American appearing in substantial opera role (5)

indicators.note: US appears inside the word for substantial

blocks.note: fat = substantial, large
US = American

annotation.surface: An American singer lands a big part at the opera house.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Substantial' seems to describe the role's size; it is the word FAT, which holds US.
annotation.definitionFit: Faust is the title role of Gounod's opera, the scholar who sells his soul.

entries.clue: Latin quarter pub introduces port (6)

indicators.note: BAR comes first, introducing RIO

blocks.note: a bar is a pub
Rio de Janeiro, the Brazilian port

annotation.surface: A tavern in the Paris student district starts serving port wine.
annotation.walkthrough: The Latin Quarter is the Paris student district, and port reads as the wine; here Latin means Spanish-speaking, and port is a harbour city.
annotation.definitionFit: A barrio is a Spanish-speaking district of a city, especially in the US.

entries.clue: Look one’s best for hearing (4)

indicators.note: the word for one's best is only to be heard, not spelt

blocks.note: at one's peak = at one's best

annotation.surface: Dressing up to look your best for a court hearing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Look one's best' reads as a single phrase; split after 'Look' to find the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to peek is to take a quick, often furtive look, as through a gap in a curtain.

entries.clue: Taking turns, both sides avoided goal (3)

indicators.note: the letters at both sides of the word are left out

blocks.note: a bendy road takes many turns; drop B and Y

annotation.surface: Players swap round, and both teams miss the target.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Taking turns' sounds like players alternating; it describes something full of bends.
annotation.definitionFit: An end is an aim or goal, as in the end justifies the means.

entries.clue: Pure blue denim knit mum wears (11)

indicators.note: the letters are knitted into a new pattern
the anagram wears SH, holding it inside

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters
mum = silent, and SH is the call for silence

annotation.surface: Mother dresses in a spotless hand-knitted blue denim outfit.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mum' is not mother but the adjective for silent, as in keep mum.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something without a single mark or flaw is pure, whether a complexion or a reputation.

entries.clue: A start on course after fellow swimmer (7)

indicators.note: 'after' places what precedes it later in the answer, so the course start and A follow the fellow

blocks.note: a fellow is a man
used as is
golfers start each hole on a golf course from the tee

annotation.surface: A golfer tees off behind a playing partner who is a keen swimmer.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Course' looks like a race or a lesson; it is a golf course.
annotation.definitionFit: The manatee is a large aquatic mammal, a slow swimmer of warm coastal waters.

entries.clue: Lit class was first to go (7)

blocks.note: a class is a kind, a sort
to be first in a race is to lead it

annotation.surface: A literature class was the first to leave.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lit' reads as short for literature; it is the past tense of light.
annotation.definitionFit: Kindled means set alight, lit.
